character.A: Complete and exact, hedges and the doubled "de plus" kept, the editors' bracket "[in] addition" kept on the right word. Idiomatic without smoothing.
character.B: Complete and fluent. One small shift of modality in the footnote; otherwise exact.
character.C: Complete and fluent. States the wished-for 2-product property as a fact; odd abbreviation "fully faith.".
character.D: First page only: complete and exact, hedges kept. Nothing to correct.
character.E: Complete and exact, very literal ("second member", "Let then", "Fumblings on"). Subjunctives kept as "be", "should have".
character.F: Complete, but with several clumsy turns ("for lack on the part of", "composed functor", "f. faithful"). States the 2-product property as a fact.
character.G: The mathematics is right, but French is left in six labels, "d'ailleurs" is dropped, a word is added and the editors' bracket is widened. The least careful of the set.
character.H: Complete and exact, impersonal "one" throughout, close to the French. Slightly heavy ("demands moreover", "equally").

conclusion: No version of either work has a major error: every sentence is translated, the formulas are intact (except Centre respelled in LM_D), and the hedges ("sans doute", "je présume", "probablement") are kept everywhere. The differences between the top versions (LM: F, H, then A, C, E, G; DER: A, D, E, then B, H) are single word choices and would not matter to a reader of an edition; the one point worth settling in the glossary is "action effective" -> "actual action", which only F and H have. Only LM_D (marks dropped or moved, untranslated \text and abbreviations) and DER_G (French left in six labels, a dropped "d'ailleurs") would need a repair pass, and DER_F is clumsier than the rest.
